options: An error, since negative indices are not valid in Python
The entire list reversed
"gpt-4o" — the first item
"gemini-pro" — negative indices count from the end of the list
questions.explain: Negative indexing counts from the end, so -1 always refers to the last item.

questions.q: What's the difference between `.append()` and `.extend()` on a list?
options: extend removes items instead of adding them
append adds a single item to the end; extend adds multiple items from another iterable
They are interchangeable with no difference
append only works on strings, not lists
questions.explain: append adds exactly one item; extend adds each item from another list or iterable individually.

questions.q: What does this list comprehension do: `[model.upper() for model in models]`?
options: Returns a single uppercase string, not a list
Modifies models in place, replacing it with uppercase values
Raises a syntax error because comprehensions require an if clause
Builds a new list where every item from models has been converted to uppercase
questions.explain: A list comprehension builds a brand-new list by applying the expression to every item in the source iterable.

questions.q: In the pattern `[m for m in models if len(m) > 8]`, what does the `if` clause do?
options: Is required syntax in every list comprehension
Stops the loop entirely the first time the condition is false
Filters the comprehension so only items matching the condition are included in the result
Only works with numbers, never strings
questions.explain: The optional if clause filters which items get included — this one keeps only model names longer than 8 characters.

questions.q: Why does this lesson connect list comprehensions directly to AI engineering work?

Because comprehensions only work with AI libraries, not plain Python
